newsitem.title: UK: Moody's may cut Dresdner, unit ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may cut Dresdner, unit ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it has placed under review for possible downgrade Dresdner Bank AG's long-term ratings (senior at Aaa) and its A bank financial strength ratings.

Moody's also said it may downgrade the long-term and financial strength ratings of Dresdner's three rated subsidiaries; Dresdner Bank Luxembourg S.A. (senior at Aa1), Banque Internationale de Placement (senior at Aa3), and Kleinwort Benson Group Plc (senior at Aa2).
"The ratings for short-term deposits and commercial paper for Dresdner and its rated subsidiaries were confirmed at Prime-1," Moody's said in a statement.

Moody's placed the following ratings under review. Dresdner Bank AG -- Aaa senior long-term debt, counterparty and deposit ratings, Aa1 subordinated debt, and A bank financial strength rating. Dresdner Australia Limited -- Aaa guaranteed senior debt. Dresdner Finance BV -- Aaa guaranteed senior debt. Dresdner International Finance Plc -- Aaa guaranteed senior debt. Banque Internationale de Placement -- Aa3 long-term deposit rating, and C bank financial strength rating. Dresdner Bank Luxembourg SA -- Aa1 long-term deposits, and B bank financial strength rating. Kleinwort Benson Group Plc -- Aa2 long-term deposits, and C bank financial strength rating.

Moody's said it initiated the rating review in the context of changing dynamics for the German banking sector -- in which tighter competition, narrower lending yields, flatter loan demand, and rising funding costs (driven by gradual savings disintermediation) were leading to a secular decline in Dresdner's traditional revenue sources.

"The review will also consider the potential new risks that have been introduced through Dresdner's focused growth strategy in asset management and certain trading and investment banking businesses," the agency said.

Moody's stated that Dresdner was characterised by a solid universal banking franchise, good asset quality, and stable earnings which were likely to keep it among the financially sounder banks worldwide.

"However, the bank's high cost structure, its more modest core capitalisation, and the rising scale of global competition are factors that may no longer be consistent with the highest ratings," Moody's said.

It said Dresdner Bank was the second largest private sector bank in Germany with group assets at September 30, 1996 of 541 billion marks ($338 billion). --Deepthi Wickremasinghe, Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041
